Connect my AI app to PublishPress. Creat:
Connect my AI app to PublishPress. Create a setup script and give me the exact terminal command to run it.

1. Ask me to select my AI app and OS (Windows, macOS or Linux). Use interactive choices if available, otherwise numbered options.
2. Create the script using your file tools. Request the specific permission if needed. If you cannot write locally, attach a downloadable script. Only fall back to code with save instructions when neither is possible. Use PowerShell on Windows and an appropriate script on macOS or Linux. Do not stop at explaining access limitations or provide only JSON.
3. Configure this local stdio server:
Name: %3$s
Display name: %4$s
Command: npx
Arguments: -y @automattic/mcp-wordpress-remote@latest
Environment: OAUTH_ENABLED=false, WP_API_URL=%1$s, WP_API_USERNAME=%2$s
Read WP_API_PASSWORD through a hidden terminal prompt.
Hub write access: %5$s. Only individually selected actions are exposed.
4. Check Node.js and npx. If missing, link to the official installer and tell me to reopen the terminal. Back up existing settings. Use a JSON/TOML parser or supported client command to merge only this server, preserving other settings and sites. Stop on invalid configuration or a conflicting endpoint. If replacing an old PublishPress desktop extension for this site, guide me to disable only that extension to avoid duplicate connections. Quote paths and values safely.
5. Give brief run, restart and approval instructions. Verify through the connection or give me a prompt to test in the app: confirm the site URL, list actual tools and perform a read-only lookup. Report whether write tools are available. If expected write tools are missing, ask me to check Allow actions that change site data and the selected actions in Hub, then refresh the connection. Do not claim success from saved configuration alone. Do not test writes during setup. Clarify the target site when ambiguous and ask for review before changing site data.

Find users by name or role. The optional: Find users by name or role. The optional primitive capability filter checks effective access within each candidate page. Visit all total_pages even when a filtered page is empty. No email addresses or secrets are returned.
Resolve exactly one user_id or username: Resolve exactly one user_id or username and return their identity, roles and effective primitive capabilities. Never guess a user ID. Object-specific permissions require a separate check for that object.
Search readable posts, pages or a REST-e: Search readable posts, pages or a REST-enabled custom post type. Returns actual IDs, titles and permalinks. Use post_type=page for pages. Resolve ambiguous titles before using a URL. Default status is publish. Private and draft requests enforce WordPress permissions.
List readable REST-enabled post types an: List readable REST-enabled post types and the capability names used for each type. Use these names for content lookups and permission questions.
Create a new user account with a known u: Create a new user account with a known username, email and one editable role. Ask for missing details. WordPress validates role assignment permissions. MCP rejects administrator and any role granting administrator-level capabilities. A password is generated privately. By default WordPress emails the user a password setup link. Never guess an email or request a password in chat.
Create a post, page or REST-enabled cust: Create a post, page or REST-enabled custom post type. Use post_type=page for pages. Defaults to draft. Publish or schedule only when requested. WordPress checks creation, publishing and author-assignment permissions. Returns the actual ID and permalink.
Edit an existing post, page or REST-enab: Edit an existing post, page or REST-enabled custom post by its verified ID. Find content first if the ID is unknown. Only supplied fields change. WordPress checks object, publishing and author-assignment permissions. No deletion, arbitrary metadata or options are supported.
